saints.name: St. Gregory of Nyssa
saints.title: Bishop
saints.shortBlurb: The youngest of the Cappadocian Fathers, a mystical theologian and champion of the Nicene faith…
biography: Born about 335 in Cappadocia, the younger brother of Basil the Great and of Macrina, Gregory first taught rhetoric and served as a reader before Basil made him bishop of the little town of Nyssa in 372. The Arians drove him out in 376 on a charge of wasting church funds, but he returned to his flock in 378, after the death of Valens.

At the Council of Constantinople in 381 he stood among the champions of the Nicene faith and preached the funeral oration of Meletius. His writings — Against Eunomius, the Great Catechetical Oration, the Life of Macrina, above all the Life of Moses — trace the soul's endless ascent into the darkness of God and make him a founder of Christian mysticism.

He was also the first writer of the ancient world to condemn slavery itself, declaring in his homilies on Ecclesiastes that no man may buy what is made in the image of God. Last heard of at a synod of Constantinople in 394, he died about 395; the Second Council of Nicaea would name him father of fathers.
saints.knownFor: His mystical theology and defense of the Nicene Creed.
